findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add the mcp `--memory 2048m` (and any other capped service run outside compose) to autodeploy.sh's `mcp_run_new` docker run and extend the compose/mcp_run_new parity oracle (test_autodeploy_mcp_bluegreen.py) to pin it, since the live mcp container is created by `docker run`, not `docker compose up`, and a compose-only mem_limit never reaches it.
evidence: docker-compose.yml:481 'MUST stay at parity with mcp_run_new in infra/scripts/autodeploy.sh (blue-green `docker run`)'
docker-compose.yml:518 '`docker run` does NOT interpolate the project .env'
autodeploy.sh:654 `mcp_run_new()` and autodeploy.sh:1154 `if ! mcp_run_new ...` is the deploy path; search for `--memory` in the repo returns (no matches)
observability.sh:1054 the mcp container '(mcp_run_new), which compose never sees'
reports/stability/ci-landing-regressions-read.md:53 records a real prior incident: a new env var 'added to compose but not to autodeploy.sh mcp_run_new' — the identical compose/run drift class
Plan D2: 'The 4.64 GB observed peak is 2.3x this limit, so that excursion now kills mcp loudly'
findings.finding: Deliverable 2's mem_limit on the compose `mcp:` service does not reach the live mcp container, because the running mcp container is created by autodeploy.sh's blue-green `docker run` (mcp_run_new), not `docker compose up` — so the 2048m limit is never in force and the plan's stated purpose ('that excursion now kills mcp loudly instead of letting the kernel choose gerrit') does not hold for the very service (mcp) whose 4.64 GB peak drives the whole plan.
scenarios: mcp's memory excursion recurs after deploy; the compose mem_limit is absent on the mcp_run_new container so the kernel OOM-killer still picks a victim by heuristic (potentially gerrit), exactly the failure the plan claims to eliminate
AC2 ('all four compose services declare mem_limit') passes on the compose file while the production mcp container remains uncapped
findings.suggested_fix: In deliverable 2, state that mcp's limit must be applied in BOTH places: `mem_limit: 2048m` on the compose service AND `--memory 2048m` on the `mcp_run_new` docker run in infra/scripts/autodeploy.sh, with the existing parity oracle extended to assert the two agree. The three compose-only services (gerrit, review-bot, opcert) are fine on the compose file alone.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add an acceptance criterion exercising the present-but-unreadable /proc/meminfo branch, asserting it emits the existing disarm marker (and defines its admit/refuse disposition).
evidence: 'present-but-unreadable emits the existing disarm marker'
AC3 covers refuse-below/admit-above; AC4 covers absent -> ADMIT; no AC references the unreadable case
findings.finding: Deliverable 3 defines four outcomes for the MemAvailable check — below floor (refuse, retryable), above floor (admit), /proc/meminfo absent (degrade to ADMIT), and present-but-unreadable (emit existing disarm marker) — but the acceptance criteria only cover three of them (AC3 refuse/admit, AC4 absent). The present-but-unreadable branch, a distinct error path on a newly-added failure point, has no acceptance/test coverage.
scenarios: A /proc/meminfo present but unreadable (permission/container-sandbox) at runtime — the disarm-marker branch ships unverified and could regress silently
findings.suggested_fix: Add AC: 'When /proc/meminfo is present but unreadable, the check emits the existing disarm marker and admits (or refuses) per the stated disposition.'

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State that both membound alarms set alarm_actions and ok_actions to aws_sns_topic.alerts.arn (the stack's existing SNS sink), so a breach actually pages.
evidence: Plan item 4 specifies only threshold, treat_missing_data, and periods for both alarms, with no mention of a notification action.
Every existing alarm in this stack sets `alarm_actions = [aws_sns_topic.alerts.arn]` and `ok_actions = [aws_sns_topic.alerts.arn]` (monitoring.tf gerrit_gate_down/disk alarms, monitoring_9ea3.tf).
An honest-alarm objective ('honest alarms' in the title) is defeated if the alarm has no sink.
findings.finding: The new membound alarms are not stated to wire alarm_actions/ok_actions to the SNS topic; without an action an alarm changes state but pages no one.
scenarios: The wedge recurs; mem_available_percent < 15 breaches but no email/SNS notification is delivered because alarm_actions was omitted.
findings.suggested_fix: Add to change 4 that each alarm sets `alarm_actions = [aws_sns_topic.alerts.arn]` and `ok_actions = [aws_sns_topic.alerts.arn]`, matching monitoring.tf's existing alarms.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Name the proving command/test for AC3/AC4 (e.g. a unit test that mocks /proc/meminfo below-floor -> retryable LLMError, above-floor -> admit, and absent-file -> admit).
evidence: AC3: 'gate_admission refuses a gate when MemAvailable is below the floor, with retryable semantics, and admits when it is above'
AC4: 'The memory check degrades to ADMIT when /proc/meminfo is absent'
No test file or command named for the new /proc/meminfo read path
findings.finding: AC3 and AC4 describe the memory-admission behavior but name no proving command/test (unlike AC5's test_alarm_window_tuning.py and AC6's terraform validate).
scenarios: An executor implements the floor but the below/above/absent branches are never exercised by a named test
findings.suggested_fix: Add to AC3/AC4 a pytest that patches the /proc/meminfo read to assert: below 1024 MiB raises a retryable LLMError (not a verdict), above admits, and FileNotFoundError degrades to ADMIT.

findings.checklist_item: Note in deliverable 3 that autodeploy.sh already reads MemAvailable at the same 1024 MiB floor with the same fail-open posture, and state explicitly why the gate-admission floor is a separate implementation (different enforcement scope) rather than a shared helper/constant.
evidence: autodeploy.sh:612 `kb="$(awk '/^MemAvailable:/{print $2}' /proc/meminfo 2>/dev/null)"`
autodeploy.sh:188 `MCP_MEM_MIN_MB="${MCP_MEM_MIN_MB:-1024}"` — same 1024 floor the plan proposes
autodeploy.sh:186-187 'Unreadable fails OPEN' — same degrade posture the plan calls 'inapplicable and stays silent' / disarm
Plan item 3: 'a MemAvailable floor read from /proc/meminfo … below 1024 MiB … Reads /proc/meminfo directly'
findings.finding: Deliverable 3's /proc/meminfo MemAvailable floor duplicates logic that already exists in infra/scripts/autodeploy.sh (mcp_mem_available_mb reads the same awk '/^MemAvailable:/' field, compares to the same 1024 MiB via MCP_MEM_MIN_MB, and fails OPEN when unreadable), and the plan does not acknowledge this prior art or state why the reading/floor is not shared.
scenarios: A future change to the memory-floor value or the meminfo parse must now be made in two places (bash deploy guard + Python admission) that can silently drift
A reviewer cannot tell whether the 1024 MiB match is intentional single-sourcing or coincidental

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Enumerate the pre-existing MemAvailable floor (autodeploy.sh MCP_MEM_MIN_MB=1024 / mcp_mem_abort metric / monitoring_foxterrier.tf mcp_mem_abort alarm) and state how Deliverables 3 and 4 relate to it (shared threshold source? overlapping alarm coverage? intentional duplication?).
evidence: autodeploy.sh:188 `MCP_MEM_MIN_MB="${MCP_MEM_MIN_MB:-1024}"` with a comment: '8 GiB t4g.large ... refuse the second container when MemAvailable is below this floor. Unreadable fails OPEN'
autodeploy.sh:606-615 `mcp_mem_available_mb()` reads `/^MemAvailable:/` from /proc/meminfo — the identical source and 1024 threshold Deliverable 3 proposes

monitoring_foxterrier.tf:109 `resource "aws_cloudwatch_metric_alarm" "mcp_mem_abort"` already alarms on the existing floor's refusals; test_alarm_window_tuning.py:349 lists mcp_mem_abort among the notBreaching counters
The plan's 'What this does NOT establish' and Deliverable 3/4 text never mention MCP_MEM_MIN_MB, mcp_mem_abort, or monitoring_foxterrier.tf
findings.finding: Deliverable 3 adds a new /proc/meminfo MemAvailable floor (1024 MiB) in gate_admission.py and Deliverable 4 adds two new mem_available_percent alarms, but the plan does not enumerate the pre-existing parallel memory floor: autodeploy.sh's MCP_MEM_MIN_MB (default 1024) reads the same /proc/meminfo:MemAvailable, refuses the blue-green second mcp container, and publishes rebar/host:mcp_mem_abort, which is already alarmed by resource mcp_mem_abort in monitoring_foxterrier.tf.
findings.location: Changes deliverables 3 and 4; infra/scripts/autodeploy.sh (MCP_MEM_MIN_MB / mcp_mem_available_mb), infra/terraform/monitoring_foxterrier.tf (mcp_mem_abort alarm)
scenarios: A reviewer or operator cannot tell whether the new gate_admission floor duplicates, supersedes, or must stay consistent with autodeploy's MCP_MEM_MIN_MB=1024 floor
The two new alarms may overlap in coverage/pager behavior with the existing mcp_mem_abort alarm on the same memory condition

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Justify (or re-target) deliverable 4's dead-man so it distinguishes probe truncation from memory silence — e.g. anchor it on the existing mem_probe_ok heartbeat or the plan's own head-present+memory-absent discriminator — rather than treating a 3h absence of a truncation-dominated tail metric as a memory signal.
evidence: Plan: 'mem_available_percent (tail) published zero datapoints for five consecutive hours' and 'absent 73-86% of the time'
Plan: 'It is SIGTERM-ed on its 240s budget before reaching the memory read'
observability.sh publishes mem_available_percent at ~line 1017 (tail) alongside a dedicated mem_probe_ok heartbeat at ~line 1022

alarm-window-tuning.md 'A limitation the 20:47Z event exposed': truncation contaminates the 'silence means the probe could not measure' premise; a reading alarm firing on absence 'should be read as the probe could not measure this, not as this generator is full'
Plan 'Corollary': 'head-metric present + memory absent = truncated ... That discrimination needs no new signal' — yet the dead-man alarm does not use it
findings.finding: Deliverable 4's dead-man alarm is built on mem_available_percent, but the plan's own measurement shows that metric's absence is dominated by probe TRUNCATION (the memory read sits at the observability.sh tail and is SIGTERM-ed before it runs), not by memory death — so a 3-hour all-empty breaching window fires on 'the probe was cut short' as readily as on 'memory pressure', which is precisely the confound alarm-window-tuning.md warns Profile-A absence alarms cannot disambiguate. The plan states the discriminator (head-metric present + memory absent = truncated) exists 'for free' but does not build the alarm on it.
findings.location: Changes → deliverable 4 (dead-man alarm); 'The probe cannot be trusted' section
scenarios: Probe is truncated for 3+ hours (the plan says this is common in the tail) while memory is healthy — the dead-man pages on truncation, reproducing the missing-data-pager the plan explicitly sets out to avoid
The one historical 3h+ all-empty window the plan cites as its sole true-positive is itself indistinguishable from a truncation storm on the same metric

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify that both membound alarms use namespace rebar/host and NO dimensions (matching how observability.sh publishes mem_available_percent), not the InstanceId+mount dimensions used by the disk alarms.
evidence: observability.sh publishes `--namespace "$NS" --metric-name mem_available_percent` with NS="rebar/host" and NO --dimensions (lines ~1017-1018).
By contrast disk_used_percent / data_disk_debris_bytes alarms in monitoring.tf carry `dimensions = { InstanceId = ..., mount = "/var/gerrit" }`.
Plan item 4 states neither namespace nor dimensions, so the binding contract for the new alarms is under-specified.
findings.finding: The plan names the metric mem_available_percent but does not state its namespace or dimensioning; the metric is published to namespace rebar/host with NO dimensions, so an alarm copied from the dimensioned disk alarms would never bind.
scenarios: The new alarm is authored with the disk-alarm InstanceId+mount dimensions (the obvious template) and silently watches a metric stream that never receives data, sitting in INSUFFICIENT_DATA / never breaching forever.
findings.suggested_fix: State in change 4 that the alarms set `namespace = "rebar/host"`, `metric_name = "mem_available_percent"`, and declare no `dimensions` block, consistent with observability.sh's undimensioned put-metric-data call.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Decide and state whether the 1024 MiB MemAvailable floor is configurable (e.g. a [snapshot] key) or justify hardcoding it in code with a rationale.
evidence: 'refusing with a retryable LLMError ... below 1024 MiB'
Alarm re-tune targets are 'recorded in the file' for the tf deliverables but no analogous config seam for the floor
findings.finding: The MemAvailable admission floor (1024 MiB) is hardcoded in gate_admission.py while the sibling alarm thresholds (15%, 3-hour window) are placed in tunable terraform files with recorded re-tune targets; the floor is equally likely to need retuning as the memory profile evolves.
scenarios: mcp steady-state grows and the 1024 MiB floor needs adjustment, requiring a code change + redeploy rather than a config edit
findings.suggested_fix: Read the floor from rebar.toml [snapshot] (e.g. mem_available_floor_mib = 1024) with the code default, mirroring how max_concurrent_gates is configured.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a one-line back-out note that the mem_limit changes are reverted by restoring the prior docker-compose.yml and redeploying (no state/data migration involved).
evidence: 'that excursion now kills mcp loudly'
'Both slots landing in one container ... OOM-kills it — a bounded, attributable failure, which is the point'
No back-out statement for the mem_limit change beyond AC6's 'Terraform is NOT applied'
findings.finding: Adding mem_limit changes production runtime behavior (kernel will now OOM-kill breaching containers) — an explicit, justified behavior change — but the plan states no rollback/back-out note for the runtime effect.
scenarios: mem_limit sizing proves too tight in practice and legitimate workloads get OOM-killed, requiring a fast revert
